title: S3: Increasing GPU Utilization during Generative Inference for Higher Throughput
technique: output-length predictor (fine-tuned DistilBERT-style bucket classifier) to right-size KV memory reservation, length-aware batching, and a supervisor that handles mispredictions by preemption

optimized_metrics.evidence: we design S3 to achieve higher throughput under those latency SLOs
S3 is a system-algorithm co-design framework that maximizes GPU utilization with sequence length prediction to achieve higher throughput
For online scenarios, we assume a latency SLO set to the average reading speed of English readers, 4 words per second [12] and 0.1875 second per token [13].
optimized_metrics.stat_quote: We next calculate the latency SLO for each sequence by multiplying 0.1875 by its sequence length (e.g., 11.25s for a sequence with 60 tokens)

headline_claim.text: Our proposed method achieves 6.49x throughput over those systems that assume the worst case for the output sequence length.

reported_metrics.where: Fig 4a (sequences/s, offline max batch), Fig 4b (online, under SLO)
predictor bucket accuracy 98.61% / 77.13% / 65.6%; model perplexity unchanged
headline only (re-pass); GPU-count saving is an evaluation result

metric_definitions.definition_quote: Fig. 4 (a) reports the maximum throughput in sequences per second for different models. We measure the throughput using the maximum batch size of each configuration.
metric_definitions.notes: throughput counts sequences/s (not tokens/s), single A100 80GB; offline = max batch size

metric_definitions.definition_quote: we assume a latency SLO set to the average reading speed of English readers, 4 words per second [12] and 0.1875 second per token [13].
metric_definitions.notes: effectively a per-token (per-iteration) latency bound of 0.1875 s; a 60-token generation is the Fig 1 workload (vertical SLO line is for reading a 60-token sequence)

slo_spec: Online scenario: latency SLO equals average reading speed, 0.1875 s per token (4 words/s); offline: loose SLO (throughput only).
load_regime: offline batch with max batch size; online = max batch size meeting SLO; no arrival-rate trace
tradeoff_acknowledged: explicit latency-throughput trade-off (Fig 1): larger batch raises throughput at the cost of higher latency; S3 aims to exploit slack below the SLO
hardware: 1x NVIDIA A100 80GB (Lenovo SD650-N V2); cost analysis with 6-10 GPUs for GPT-3
workloads: Alpaca dataset (predictor fine-tuned on Alpaca; also Natural-Questions and a QA set for predictor accuracy)
extractor_notes: Baseline is Orca assuming max-sequence-length reservation, not vLLM. Latency SLO is per-token (reading speed) mean, not a percentile. Throughput unit is sequences/s. Memory is the lever (batch size), but MEMORY is not itself the metric reported.
